On the Same Day, Three Conditional Approvals: OCC Turns Stablecoin Bank Authorization into 'Standard Parts' | HTX InsightsHomeCrypto News以太坊On the Same Day, Three Conditi...On the Same Day, Three Conditional Approvals: OCC Turns Stablecoin Bank Authorization into 'Standard Parts'marsbitPublished on 2026-09-23Last updated on 2026-09-23AbstractOn September 18th, the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) granted conditional approvals to three institutions—Agora, Catena, and Bastion—for federal trust bank charters focused on stablecoin-related activities. These approvals indicate the OCC is establishing a replicable regulatory pathway for non-deposit-taking "narrow" trust banks. However, significant execution and legal hurdles remain, including final authorization for Agora and Catena to begin operations, a charter conversion for Bastion, ongoing state-level legal challenges, and pending stablecoin legislation.

The OCC applied a standardized regulatory framework across all three approvals, setting capital requirements, mandating liquidity to cover 180 days of operational costs, and emphasizing robust compliance, audit, and governance structures. While the federal charter reduces regulatory fragmentation, its increasing availability diminishes its value as a standalone competitive advantage. The key differentiators for success will now be final execution, distribution channels, capital and reserve partnerships, and overall operational performance. The business models of the three firms vary: Agora focuses on institutional stablecoin issuance and custody, Catena targets AI-driven agent services, and Bastion provides white-label enterprise infrastructure. Europe to Test Interlinking Its Payment System With Brazil’s Pix

The ECB is taking the first steps to expand its payments infrastructure by linking its systems to other international payment networks.

On Thursday, the bank announced that it was evaluating the feasibility of interlinking the TARGET Instant Payment Settlement (TIPS) platform with Brazil’s Pix, a national rapid payment network, as part of the G20 cross-border payments roadmap. In a press release, the institution declared it would “explore the potential for interlinking TIPS and Pix by assessing technical, operational, legal, and business considerations” in close collaboration with the Central Bank of Brazil.

As economic flows between the EU and Brazil grow, the ECB highlighted that this connection could enable faster, lower-cost instant payments for both retail and institutional users in the two regions. Brazil is the EU’s tenth-largest partner, with over €87 billion (nearly $100 billion) in bilateral trade registered in 2025.

While TIPS currently settles real-time payments in euros, Swedish krona, and Danish krone, it can also be adapted to use multiple other currencies, potentially allowing the inclusion of Brazilian reais.

A combined EU-Brazil system could represent an alternative to SWIFT settlements, reducing dependence on U.S. dollar-controlled networks. The U.S. has heavily criticized Pix, pointing out that it drives competitors out of the Brazilian payments market as it facilitates over 250 million payments daily settled with low fees.
